# Choosing a Test {#sec-choosing-a-test .unnumbered}

```{r, include = FALSE}
source("global_stuff.R")
```

Start at the top of @fig-choose-test with the kind of outcome you measured, then follow the questions down to a test. In the web version of the book, each test in the chart links to its test card, a short table in its chapter that gives the test's purpose, hypotheses, assumptions, test statistic and what to report. Pearson correlation has no card, because Chapter 2 introduces it without a formal test, so it links to its section instead.

::: {.column-screen-inset}

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-choose-test
%%| fig-cap: "Choosing a test, organized by the kind of outcome (DV), then by the design. In the web version, click a test to open its test card."
%%| fig-alt: "Flowchart. The top question asks what kind of outcome you have. Categorical counts split into one categorical variable, leading to the chi-square goodness-of-fit test, and two categorical variables, leading to the chi-square test of independence. A continuous outcome splits into two questions. A relationship between two continuous variables leads to Pearson correlation for the association alone, or simple linear regression to predict. Comparing means across groups asks whether there is a continuous covariate to control for. If yes, ANCOVA. If no, the next question is how many groups and factors. One group against a reference, or paired before-and-after measurements, leads to the one-sample or paired t-test when assumptions are met and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test when they are violated. Two independent groups lead to the independent-samples t-test or the Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon test. Three or more groups with one factor lead to one-way ANOVA, followed by Tukey HSD if significant, or the Kruskal-Wallis test. Two or more categorical factors at once lead to factorial ANOVA."
flowchart TD

  CAT --> C2["Two categorical variables"] --> IND["Chi-square test of independence<br/>(Ch 7)"]
  CON --> R1["Relationship between two continuous variables?"]
  R1 -->|just the association| COR["Pearson correlation<br/>(Ch 2)"]
  R1 -->|want to predict| REG["Simple linear regression<br/>(Ch 9)"]
  CON --> M1["Compare means across groups?"] --> CV["Is there a continuous covariate to control for?"]
  CV -->|Yes| ANC["ANCOVA<br/>(Ch 11)"]
  CV -->|No| G["How many groups, and how many factors?"]
  G --> G1["1 group vs. a reference, or paired (before/after)"]
  G --> G2["2 independent groups"]
  G --> G3["3+ groups, one factor"]
  G --> G4["2+ categorical factors at once"]
  G1 -->|assumptions met| T1["One-sample t-test<br/>(Ch 6)"]
  G1 -->|assumptions met| TP["Paired t-test<br/>(Ch 6)"]
  G1 -->|assumptions violated| WSR["Wilcoxon signed-rank test<br/>(Ch 7)"]
  G2 -->|assumptions met| TI["Independent-samples t-test<br/>(Ch 6)"]
  G2 -->|assumptions violated| MWW["Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon test<br/>(Ch 7)"]
  G3 -->|assumptions met| AOV["One-way ANOVA<br/>(Ch 8)"]
  G3 -->|assumptions violated| KW["Kruskal-Wallis test<br/>(Ch 8)"]
  AOV -->|if significant| TK["Tukey HSD post-hoc<br/>(Ch 8)"]
  G4 --> FAC["Factorial ANOVA<br/>(Ch 10)"]
```

:::

@tbl-all-tests lists every test in the book with the chapter that teaches it and a link to its card, or for Pearson correlation, its section.

| Test | Use it when | Chapter | Card or section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pearson correlation | You want the strength and direction of a linear relationship between two continuous variables | 2 | @sec-2pearson |
| One-sample $t$-test | You compare one sample mean with a reference value | 6 | @tbl-6card-onesample |
| Paired $t$-test | You measure the same units twice | 6 | @tbl-6card-paired |
| Independent-samples $t$-test | You compare the means of two separate groups | 6 | @tbl-6card-indep |
| Wilcoxon signed-rank test | One-sample or paired data, when normality is doubtful | 7 | @tbl-7card-signedrank |
| Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon test | Two separate groups, when normality is doubtful | 7 | @tbl-7card-mww |
| Chi-square goodness-of-fit test | Counts for one categorical variable, compared with an expected pattern | 7 | @tbl-7card-gof |
| Chi-square test of independence | Two categorical variables measured on the same units | 7 | @tbl-7card-indep |
| One-way ANOVA | Three or more groups, one factor | 8 | @tbl-8card-anova |
| Kruskal-Wallis test | Three or more groups, when residuals are skewed in a small sample | 8 | @tbl-8card-kw |
| Simple linear regression | You want to predict a continuous outcome from one continuous predictor | 9 | @tbl-9card-regression |
| Factorial ANOVA | Two or more categorical factors at once | 10 | @tbl-10card-factorial |
| ANCOVA | Groups compared while a continuous covariate is in the model | 11 | @tbl-11card-ancova |

: Every test in the book. {#tbl-all-tests}
